name: Rust Parser Libraries
description: Libraries and tools for building parsers in Rust — parser combinators, parser/lexer generators, PEG frameworks, and incremental/lossless syntax-tree toolkits — compared across parsing model, input/output, diagnostics, editor support, performance, Rust integration, and ecosystem, with a focus on language and DSL frontends

groups.name: General Information
groups.description: Licensing, parsing approach, implementation, and basic identifying information

attributes.name: License
attributes.description: From Cargo.toml / LICENSE; dual-licensed projects carry both tags

attributes.name: Approach
attributes.description: Dominant parsing style; a second tag only when genuinely dual (e.g. pest = grammar file + PEG)

attributes.name: Implementation
attributes.description: Pure Rust (no C/C++ in the dependency tree) vs bindings to a native engine

attributes.name: Repository
attributes.description: Primary source repository

attributes.name: Crates.io
attributes.description: Package page of the main/umbrella crate

attributes.name: Documentation
attributes.description: docs.rs or dedicated book/site (book preferred when one exists)

attributes.name: First Release
attributes.description: Year of first crates.io publish

attributes.name: Latest Stable Version
attributes.description: Current non-prerelease version on crates.io; date checked noted in comment

groups.name: Parsing Model
groups.description: Grammar class, how the grammar is defined, and how recursion, ambiguity, and lexing are handled

attributes.name: Grammar Class
attributes.description: What the tool can parse; combinators impose no formal class and get 'Arbitrary'

attributes.name: Grammar Definition
attributes.description: Where the grammar lives: plain Rust, inside a macro, or a separate grammar file

attributes.name: Left Recursion
attributes.description: Directly supported, via a Pratt/precedence helper, must be eliminated by hand, or not applicable (lexers)

attributes.name: Ambiguity Handling
attributes.description: LR conflicts fail generation, PEG first-match, GLR forests, or combinator alternatives

attributes.name: Backtracking
attributes.description: Unlimited, bounded via a cut/commit operator, or none (deterministic table-driven)

attributes.name: Lexer Integration
attributes.description: Scannerless/bundled lexer, accepts any token iterator, designed to pair with a named lexer, or is itself a lexer

attributes.name: Precedence / Pratt Support
attributes.description: Dedicated operator-precedence facility (chumsky::pratt, pest PrattParser, LALRPOP %left/%right)

attributes.name: Unicode-Aware
attributes.description: Handles UTF-8 boundaries correctly and offers char-level primitives, not just bytes

groups.name: Input & Output
groups.description: Accepted input types, streaming, zero-copy, spans, and the shape of the parse result

attributes.name: Input Types
attributes.description: Input representations the parser can consume

attributes.name: Streaming / Partial Input
attributes.description: Can parse incomplete input and signal 'need more' (nom Incomplete, winnow Partial)

attributes.name: Zero-Copy
attributes.description: Output can borrow from the input without allocating

attributes.name: Span Tracking
attributes.description: Span information available on parse results; note opt-in wrapper types (e.g. nom_locate) in comment

attributes.name: Output Model
attributes.description: User-built Rust types, untyped pairs/nodes, green/red trees with trivia, or a token stream

attributes.name: Semantic Actions
attributes.description: How values are built: arbitrary Rust in grammar actions, walking a generic tree afterwards, or .map()/.then() chains

attributes.name: Whitespace / Comment Handling
attributes.description: Implicit WHITESPACE/COMMENT rules, explicit combinators, skipped by the lexer, or preserved as trivia

attributes.name: Stateful Parsing
attributes.description: Supports threading user state (symbol tables, indentation stack) through the parse

groups.name: Error Handling & Diagnostics
groups.description: Recovery, multi-error reporting, span fidelity, and integration with diagnostic crates

attributes.name: Error Recovery
attributes.description: Stop at first error, skip-to-sync-token, user-defined strategies, or built-in repair (grmtools CPCT+, tree-sitter ERROR nodes)

attributes.name: Multiple Errors Per Parse
attributes.description: Can report more than one error from a single run

attributes.name: Expected-Token Reporting
attributes.description: Errors carry the set of tokens/rules valid at the failure point

attributes.name: Custom Error Types
attributes.description: User can substitute their own error type

attributes.name: Error Span Fidelity
attributes.description: 5 = byte-range spans with labelled secondary spans; 4 = byte-range; 3 = single offset; 2 = line only; 1 = message text only

attributes.name: Diagnostic Crate Integration
attributes.description: Documented or first-party bridge to a diagnostic rendering crate

attributes.name: Contextual Error Messages
attributes.description: Mechanism to attach human-readable labels/context to sub-parsers or rules (nom context, chumsky labelled, LALRPOP error tokens)

attributes.name: Incremental Reparsing
attributes.description: Can reuse the previous tree when the input is edited

attributes.name: Lossless Syntax Tree
attributes.description: Retains whitespace/comments so the source can be reconstructed exactly

attributes.name: Syntax Highlighting Queries
attributes.description: Ships a query/pattern language or API designed for highlighting and code navigation

attributes.name: Used by an LSP / IDE
attributes.description: Verified production editor uses; cite the consuming project's Cargo.toml or docs

groups.name: Performance
groups.description: Runtime speed tier, compile-time cost, allocation behaviour, and generated code size

attributes.name: Runtime Speed Tier
attributes.description: Top tier = within ~1.5x of hand-written; fast = 1.5–3x; moderate = 3–10x; slow = >10x. Requires an independent or reproducible benchmark

attributes.name: Compile-Time Impact
attributes.description: Incremental build cost from deep generic instantiation or large generated tables; cite measurements or issues

attributes.name: Allocation Strategy
attributes.description: Whether parsing can avoid heap allocation, works with arenas, or allocates per node

attributes.name: Generated Code Size
attributes.description: Generators only; N/A for combinators

groups.name: Rust Integration
groups.description: no_std, MSRV, unsafe usage, proc-macro and build.rs reliance, dependency footprint, WASM and async friendliness

attributes.name: no_std Support
attributes.description: Compiles without std (with or without alloc — note which in comment)

attributes.name: MSRV
attributes.description: Minimum supported Rust version from Cargo.toml rust-version or README

attributes.name: Unsafe Usage
attributes.description: #![forbid(unsafe_code)], a few audited blocks, substantial unsafe, or FFI bindings to C

attributes.name: Proc-Macro Reliance
attributes.description: Whether procedural macros are needed to use the library

attributes.name: build.rs Step
attributes.description: Requires a build script to generate code (LALRPOP, tree-sitter grammar compilation)

attributes.name: Dependency Count
attributes.description: Direct non-dev dependencies of the main (runtime) crate; lower is better

attributes.name: WASM Compatible
attributes.description: Compiles to wasm32-unknown-unknown and/or WASI without special setup

attributes.name: Async-Friendly
attributes.description: Parsers/results are Send and usable with async input sources without wrapper hacks

groups.name: Ecosystem & Maintenance
groups.description: Popularity, release activity, maintenance status, documentation, and notable adopters

attributes.name: GitHub Stars
attributes.description: Snapshot; date noted in comment

attributes.name: Crates.io Downloads
attributes.description: All-time downloads of the main crate

attributes.name: Last Release
attributes.description: Most recent crates.io publish

attributes.name: Maintenance Status
attributes.description: Active = release or substantive commit in last 6 months; passive = bug fixes only for 12+ months; name successor in comment when superseded

attributes.name: Documentation Quality
attributes.description: 5 = book + comprehensive API docs + cookbook + migration guides; 3 = solid API docs with examples; 1 = minimal or stale

attributes.name: Tutorial / Book
attributes.description: Has a dedicated long-form guide beyond API docs

attributes.name: Notable Users
attributes.description: 2–4 well-known projects using it, with links in source

attributes.name: Bus Factor
attributes.description: Single maintainer, 2–5 contributors, or company-backed / large team
